entities.name: NBC News
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
NBC News, the news division of the National Broadcasting Company (NBC), founded as a radio network in 1926 by RCA and operating as a television news organization since NBC's first experimental broadcasts in the late 1930s and regular broadcasts from 1939, is one of the three major American broadcast news organizations (alongside CBS News and ABC News) and historically one of the most significant news institutions in the United States — home to David Brinkley, Chet Huntley, Tom Brokaw, and the pioneering evening news formats that shaped American television journalism.

NBC News' broadcast history includes landmark television journalism: the Huntley-Brinkley Report (1956-1970) was the dominant evening news broadcast of its era, pioneering the co-anchor format; the 1963 Kennedy assassination coverage demonstrated television news's capacity for continuous breaking news; and Tom Brokaw's 1989 Berlin Wall fall coverage became defining television news moments. NBC's Today show (premiering 1952) is the longest-running US morning news program.

In the cable era, NBC News expanded through MSNBC (launched 1996 in partnership with Microsoft) — which became America's leading left-center cable news network under Rachel Maddow, Brian Williams, and other anchors. NBC Nightly News with Lester Holt continues the legacy of Brinkley, Huntley, and Brokaw. NBC News is now part of NBCUniversal, a Comcast subsidiary. The network's extraordinary archive of American history coverage — from Eisenhower through Obama to Trump — makes it one of the most significant documentary records of 20th-21st century American life.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: NBC News — pioneering the co-anchor format, covering Kennedy's assassination, anchoring the Berlin Wall fall, and extending through MSNBC to become America's leading left-center cable network — is one of America's most historically significant broadcast journalism institutions.
